title: Two selected field-kinematics dust candidates show W2 reversals within the same NEOWISE season
abstract: We test monotone infrared evolution in 20 published centred W2-variable extreme-dust candidates. Each seasonal sequence has its own monotone curve and its own direction. A conservative Gaussian error bound rejects this null for eight selected stars, including two of seven with field kinematics, with a 0.03 mag error floor and a threshold of 0.05/180. Gaia DR3 5494787133356311680 and 6439523047616469888 retain rejection after any one visit is removed. Same-season W2 triples show turnarounds of 0.665 and 0.733 mag. With a 0.05 mag marginal error floor, simultaneous lower bounds are 0.171 and 0.162 mag. Both targets also pass a tested covariance envelope at a 0.03 mag floor. Constant offsets between seasonal viewing directions cannot explain these reversals. A variable blend or changing scan-dependent contamination remains possible. The result constrains monotone fixed-spectrum decay if the signal belongs to the stars; it does not prove recurrent dust production or old ages. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and local retrieval instructions are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-12178d7d24b3; topic astronomy; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
